correctness.rationale: A changed 111 center has only original 11 adjacent pairs, so no witnessing edge can be destroyed, and code size is preserved by replacement. On 111-free words, an interior discrepancy would force neighboring ones on the word having a one, contradicting the constraint. Therefore nondistinguishability is exactly the boundary-projection fiber relation, and R_n is an optimal transversal. The four-state transfer matrix has characteristic polynomial λ(λ³−λ²−λ−1), giving all initial values, recurrence, and generating function; two standard-library verifiers completed and agree. Boundary n=2 separately checked. All conclusions follow symbolically for every n≥2; finite tests do not substitute for proof.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural finite-blocklength zero-error packing problem for all block lengths in a classical one-memory channel: asymptotic exponential capacity alone does not determine M_F(n). It identifies the confusability quotient of the complete 111-free language, an optimal explicit code and a rational generating function allowing exact sizing at any length; this is not merely a small finite enumeration, an arbitrary parameter slice or an exponent restatement.
